feedback.worked_solution:
Remember that in general, if a point $A$ has coordinates $({a}_{x},{a}_{y},{a}_{z}),$ then its position vector is given by

$$
\overset{\to }{OA}=⟨{a}_{x},{a}_{y},{a}_{z}⟩.
$$

Here, the point $P$ has coordinates $(0,0,3),$ so its position vector is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}p & =⟨0,0,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The point $Q$ has coordinates $(0,-3,2),$ so its position vector is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}q & =⟨0,-3,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The point $R$ has coordinates $(0,4,3),$ so its position vector is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =⟨0,4,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$
